subChunks.title: Shadows and Effects
subChunks.hookHtml: Shadows, filters, and blending effects create the depth and atmosphere that separate polished UIs from flat ones. Tailwind's shadow scale, drop-shadow filters, and backdrop utilities let you build elevated cards, frosted glass effects, and depth cues without writing any CSS.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Box shadow

shadow-none  /* removes shadow                */
shadow-sm    /* very subtle — 1px elevation   */
shadow       /* default — card-level          */
shadow-md    /* moderate — floating element   */
shadow-lg    /* prominent — dropdown          */
shadow-xl    /* strong — modal                */
shadow-2xl   /* dramatic — overlays           */
shadow-inner /* inset shadow — recessed look  */

/* Coloured shadows */
shadow-blue-500/20   /* blue-tinted shadow at 20% opacity */

Drop shadow (filter-based, for non-rectangular shapes)

/* Works on PNG icons, SVGs with transparency: */
drop-shadow-sm
drop-shadow
drop-shadow-md
drop-shadow-lg
drop-shadow-xl
drop-shadow-none

Backdrop filter (frosted glass)

/* Frosted glass effect: */
<div class="backdrop-blur-md bg-white/20 border border-white/30 rounded-xl p-6">
  <!-- content visible through the blur -->
</div>

backdrop-blur-sm   backdrop-blur   backdrop-blur-md   backdrop-blur-lg   backdrop-blur-xl
backdrop-brightness-75  /* darken behind */
backdrop-saturate-150   /* enhance colour behind */

Filter effects

blur-sm   blur   blur-md   blur-lg   blur-xl   blur-none
brightness-50   brightness-75   brightness-100   brightness-125   brightness-150
contrast-50     contrast-75     contrast-100     contrast-125
grayscale       /* fully desaturated     */
grayscale-0     /* no grayscale (reset)  */
sepia           /* warm sepia tone       */
invert          /* colour inversion      */
hue-rotate-90

Transform effects

scale-95   scale-100   scale-105   scale-110   scale-150
-translate-x-1   translate-x-2   translate-y-4
rotate-45   rotate-90   rotate-180   -rotate-6
skew-x-6   skew-y-3

Common design patterns

/* Elevated card */
<div class="bg-white rounded-2xl shadow-lg hover:shadow-xl transition-shadow duration-200">

/* Frosted glass nav */
<nav class="sticky top-0 z-30
            backdrop-blur-md bg-white/80
            border-b border-gray-200/50">

/* Image with grayscale on hover (portfolio style) */
<img class="grayscale hover:grayscale-0 transition-all duration-300">

/* Loading skeleton shimmer */
<div class="bg-gray-200 rounded animate-pulse h-4 w-3/4"></div>

Sable: "backdrop-blur is the modern way to create depth without blocking content. It is used extensively in macOS, iOS, and modern SaaS products. The pattern is always the same: backdrop-blur-md bg-white/70 border border-white/20. That combination creates the frosted glass effect used in high-end product UIs."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: Shadows communicate elevation. A card is shadow-md. A dropdown is shadow-lg. A modal is shadow-xl. The shadow scale is a vocabulary of depth — learn it once and you will know instinctively which shadow belongs on which element.

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a profile card with depth: a shadow that increases on hover with a subtle upward movement, a member avatar with a grayscale filter that animates to full colour on hover, a skeleton loading state for the card content (three animated placeholder lines), and a frosted glass overlay that appears on hover covering the bottom third of the card.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between shadow (box-shadow) and drop-shadow (filter: drop-shadow) — when should you use each? Walk through the frosted glass pattern: what does each of backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/80, and border-white/20 contribute to the visual effect?

questions.prompt: Which class creates a pulsing animation used for skeleton loading states?
questions.explanation: animate-pulse applies a CSS animation that fades the element's opacity between 100% and 50% repeatedly. Combined with bg-gray-200 and rounded on a div, it creates the skeleton loading effect used in modern UIs while content loads.

questions.prompt: You want a navigation bar that blurs the content behind it (frosted glass effect). Which class combination achieves this?
options: backdrop-blur-md bg-white/80 — blurs what's behind and uses a semi-transparent white background
blur-md bg-white/80 — blur the nav itself and make it transparent
filter-blur-md bg-white opacity-80 — applies filter to the nav
background-blur bg-white/80 — CSS background blur shorthand
questions.answer: backdrop-blur-md bg-white/80 — blurs what's behind and uses a semi-transparent white background
questions.explanation: backdrop-blur-md applies the backdrop-filter: blur() CSS property, which blurs the content behind the element. The element itself needs a semi-transparent background (bg-white/80) to show the blur effect — a fully opaque background would hide the blur. blur-md would blur the nav's own content, which is the opposite of what you want.

questions.prompt: You want a PNG icon with a transparent background to have a coloured glow/shadow effect that follows its exact shape. Should you use shadow-* or drop-shadow-*?
options: drop-shadow-* — it's a CSS filter that traces the actual visible pixels of the image, including transparency
shadow-* — box-shadow is more performant than filter
Both work identically for PNG images
shadow-* with rounded-none to prevent clipping
questions.answer: drop-shadow-* — it's a CSS filter that traces the actual visible pixels of the image, including transparency
questions.explanation: box-shadow (shadow-*) creates a shadow behind the element's rectangular bounding box — for a PNG with a transparent background, you'd see a rectangular shadow, not one that follows the icon shape. drop-shadow as a CSS filter traces the actual opaque pixels, creating a shadow that follows the icon's visual outline. For icons, logos, and illustrated characters: drop-shadow. For cards and containers: shadow.
